cards.text: Saul and his son Jonathan are dead, and David has poured out his grief for them in a song (2 Samuel 1:17-27). Some time later, David doesn't just pack up and make a move. He asks the LORD first: should he go up to one of the towns of Judah?

cards.question: When David asks about going up to a town of Judah, the LORD tells him to wait.
David asks a follow-up question: where should he go? The LORD answers: go to ___.

cards.text: Two questions, two answers, and David heads up to Hebron, but not alone. Baker, I have spent LONGER than that deciding between sprinkles and chocolate chips.

cards.question: Who goes with David to Hebron?

answers.text: His two wives Ahinoam and Abigail
His father Jesse and his brothers
The prophet Samuel and the priests

cards.text: David's men come along too, every one of them with his whole household. That's not moving day, friend, that's a PARADE, and they all settle in the towns near Hebron.

cards.question: Then the men of Judah come to David in Hebron. What do they do there?

answers.text: Anoint him king over the house of Judah
Ask him to lead them against the Philistines
Hand him the crown from Saul's head

cards.question: In Hebron, the men of Judah anoint David king over every tribe of Israel.

cards.text: Then the men of Judah pass along some news. Saul fell in battle on Mount Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:1-6), and someone gave him a burial.

cards.question: The men of Judah tell David that the men of ___ buried Saul.

cards.text: So David sends messengers to Jabesh-gilead with a message. No text, no group chat, friend. He sends REAL PEOPLE to carry it all the way there, and here I am, too lazy to walk a note across my own bakery.

cards.question: What message does David send to the men of Jabesh-gilead?

answers.text: The LORD bless you for your kindness to Saul
The LORD guard you as you mourn for Saul
The LORD reward you for joining my army

cards.question: David's message tells the men of Jabesh-gilead may the LORD show them loving devotion, and David promises to show them favor too because of what they did.
David tells the men of Jabesh-gilead to be strong and courageous. What reason does he give them?

answers.text: Saul is dead but Judah has anointed David king
The Philistines are marching toward their town
The LORD has promised them a great victory

cards.text: Meanwhile, Saul's side is NOT just sitting around. Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, is about to make a big move.

cards.question: Abner, the commander of Saul's army, takes someone and moves him to Mahanaim. Who is it?
Abner makes Ish-bosheth king over Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim and Benjamin. That's king over all ___.
Now that Ish-bosheth is king over all Israel, the house of Judah follows him instead of David.
Ish-bosheth is forty when he begins to reign over Israel, and he reigns for two years. How long is David king in Hebron over the house of Judah?

cards.text: Hold on to your apron, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The card uses verse 1 for "Two questions, two answers" and for the destination Hebron, as well as verse 2 for David going there, but it cites only 2 Samuel 2:2. Its citation should span 2 Samuel 2:1-2.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the narration about the messengers, "No text, no group chat, friend.", and the final joke. Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
